radiology_report:
Subject: Prostate mpMRI | Date: 18 Feb 2025 | Facility: Amsterdam UMC VUmc
Clinical context: Assessment of a 1.6 ng/mL prostate-specific antigen level alongside a previous PI-RADS 2 categorization.
Imaging characteristics: The gland occupies 32.0 mL of space. The peripheral compartment shows standard T2 intensity with benign-apparent diffusion restriction. Within the transition compartment, mild nodular enlargement is present, lacking any focal mass effect. A discrete 8 mm focus located in the left mid-gland transition zone exhibits uniform T2 brightness, absent diffusion limitation, and negative contrast kinetics. Extracapsular spread and seminal vesicle involvement are conspicuously absent. Pelvic adenopathy is not observed.
IMPRESSION:
1. Glandular capacity: 32.0 mL.
2. PI-RADS 2 lesion in the left mid-gland transition zone, diameter ~8 mm.
3. Absence of PI-RADS 3+ pathology.
4. PSAD 0.06 ng/mL/mL.
5. csPCa predicted probability 0.6872062.

previous_notes.author: Dr. R. Visser (GP)
previous_notes.text: Laboratory tracking reveals a slow ascent, climbing from 0.9 ng/mL during 2022 to 1.1 ng/mL by the middle of the following year. Only slight lower urinary tract complaints are reported, with no acute complications noted.

previous_notes.author: Dr. R. Visser (GP)
previous_notes.text: Recent assays place the antigen concentration at 1.5 ng/mL. Noting the consistent upward curve and the gentleman's apprehension about invasive testing, a specialist urology consultation alongside dedicated imaging was organized. Pharmacological regimen remains stable.
